what_it_does: Modern AI chips often use chiplets—small specialized chips bonded together onto a glass-like interposer that routes signals between them. This paper introduces SHINSAI, a smarter interposer that acts like a flexible postal service between different top-level chips. The key innovation is programmable routing fabric: instead of hard-wiring connections for one specific chip combination, this interposer has reconfigurable switching that lets you rewire how chips talk to each other. It also includes on-board memory (512 megabits of fast SRAM) so data doesn't have to travel far. This makes the same interposer reusable across many different chip designs, whereas old interposers were custom-made for each configuration.
